note: One entry per official FAA form. `url` is filled in by `python src/scripts/capstone.py sync-form-links --write`, which finds each form's link in the AME guide's own hyperlinks and checks that it works; `urlSource` is `guide` when the URL came from the guide and `manual` when the guide does not link the form and a person entered it. To add a form, give it an id, title, summary, completedBy and `match` phrases, leave `url` empty, and run the sync. `match` holds the phrases the guide uses for the form, compared after lower-casing and normalising dashes and spacing (see normalizeFormText in src/packages/content/forms.ts). `conditions` attaches a form to a whole condition when no table row names it.

forms.title: Eyes – Refractive Surgery Status Summary
forms.summary: A two-page sheet about your LASIK, SMILE or PRK eye surgery: when it was done, how your eyes healed, and your vision now.

forms.title: Eyes – Lens Implant Status Summary
forms.summary: A two-page sheet about surgery that replaced the lens of your eye, such as cataract surgery with a lens implant: when it was done, how your eyes healed, and your vision now.

forms.title: Amblyopia (Lazy Eye) Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about your lazy eye and how well you see. You can hand in this sheet or a detailed progress note that covers the same points.

forms.title: Chorioretinitis Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about swelling at the back of your eye (chorioretinitis) and how it affects your vision. You can hand in this sheet or a detailed progress note that covers the same points.

forms.title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about your COPD, your treatment and your breathing test results. Hand it in together with a detailed progress note.
forms.completedBy: Your lung doctor, or the doctor who manages your COPD

forms.title: Sarcoid or Sarcoidosis Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about your sarcoidosis and how it is being treated. You can hand in this sheet or a detailed progress note that covers the same points.
forms.completedBy: Your lung doctor, or the doctor who treats your sarcoidosis

forms.title: Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation (AFib)/A-Flutter Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about your irregular heartbeat (AFib or atrial flutter) and how it is being treated. You can hand in this sheet or a detailed progress note that covers the same points.

forms.title: Typical Atrial Flutter Treated with Ablation Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about the ablation procedure used to treat your atrial flutter and how your heart has been since. You can hand in this sheet or a detailed progress note that covers the same points.

forms.title: Pacemaker Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about your pacemaker: the device, its settings and its latest check. You can hand in this sheet or records that cover the same points.

forms.title: Deep Brain Stimulator (DBS) Status Summary
forms.summary: A sheet about your deep brain stimulator and its current settings. It is the second page of this PDF; the first page is the FAA's table for the condition. If you have two devices, fill in one sheet for each.

forms.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) Treated Status Report
forms.summary: A one-page report on your sleep apnea treatment. You fill in the first two items and sign, then the provider who treats your sleep apnea finishes it.
forms.completedBy: You, then the provider who treats your sleep apnea

forms.title: PATH Status Summary – Anxiety, Depression, and Related Conditions
forms.summary: A one-page sheet for pilots the FAA has placed in its PATH program. Use it only if you already have a special issuance or special consideration letter that says you are in PATH.

forms.title: Coronary Heart Disease (CHD)/Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) Recertification Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet for renewing a medical certificate with heart artery disease. Use it only if you already have a special issuance for this condition.

forms.title: Diabetes or Hyperglycemia on Medications Status Report
forms.summary: A one-page report on diabetes or high blood sugar treated with medicine other than insulin. Do not use it if you take any type of insulin.
forms.completedBy: The provider who treats your diabetes

forms.title: Diabetes on Insulin Re-Certification Status Report (Non-CGM, Third Class Option)
forms.summary: A two-page report on diabetes treated with insulin, for pilots who do not use a continuous glucose monitor and are applying for a third-class certificate.
forms.completedBy: The provider who treats your diabetes
match: diabetes on insulin re-certification status report

forms.title: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)/Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma (SLL) Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about your CLL or SLL and how it is being managed. Hand it in together with a detailed progress note and your lab results.

forms.title: Low Testosterone (Low T) Hypogonadism Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about your low testosterone and its treatment. You can hand in this sheet or a detailed progress note that covers the same points.
forms.completedBy: Your urologist, endocrinologist, or treating doctor

forms.title: Weight Loss Management or Prediabetes Status Report
forms.summary: A one-page report on medicine you take for weight loss or prediabetes.
forms.completedBy: The provider who prescribes the medicine

forms.title: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ)/Chloroquine (CQ) Status Summary
forms.summary: A one-page sheet about eye checks while you take hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine (Plaquenil or Aralen).
forms.completedBy: The eye doctor who monitors your medicine

forms.title: Alcohol Event Status Report for the AME
forms.summary: A one-page report your medical examiner fills in after an alcohol-related arrest or detainment, based on your exam and records. You do not fill it in, but it shows what the examiner will ask about.

forms.title: FAA Airman Seizure Questionnaire
forms.summary: A three-page list of questions about any seizures you have had. If they happened when you were a child, a parent or guardian who saw them should answer.

forms.title: Quality of Vision Questionnaire
forms.summary: A one-page list of questions about vision problems such as glare, halos or blurred vision. Bring the finished page to your medical examiner.

forms.title: Berlin Questionnaire (Sleep Apnea)
forms.summary: A short list of questions about snoring and daytime tiredness, used to judge your risk of sleep apnea. Your medical examiner may go through it with you.

forms.title: STOP BANG Questionnaire (Sleep Apnea)
forms.summary: Eight yes-or-no questions used to judge your risk of sleep apnea. Your medical examiner may go through it with you.

forms.title: FAA Form 8500-7, Report of Eye Evaluation
forms.summary: The FAA's official eye exam report. Take it to your eye appointment and bring back the finished form.

forms.title: Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) – FAA Result Sheet
forms.summary: A one-page sheet for recording the results of a six-minute walk test, which measures how far you can walk in six minutes.
forms.completedBy: The provider who treats your heart or lung condition

forms.title: Pilot Information – Current, Detailed Clinical Progress Note
forms.summary: Not a form to fill in. It lists what your doctor's visit note must include for the FAA to accept it. A patient-portal printout or after-visit summary is usually not enough, so share this with your doctor.
forms.completedBy: Your treating doctor writes the note
